text:
Alex: noticed a sharp tail increase on the attention path after yesterday's runtime tweak. p99 jumped from ~42ms to ~120ms on the paged->flash fallback case.

Priya: ugh, saw that too. Is this the kernel selector change that prefers fused_attn for seq>512?

Alex: seems correlated. traces show an extra kernel handoff at seq=768 where we split to flash_variant_b then fallback to paged_attn. timeline:
```
flash_variant_b launch 0.9ms
paged_attn warmup 45ms
KV cache lookup 2ms
overall token 120ms
```

Jamal: can you post the bisect range? I can run targeted bench.

Alex: bisect between commit abc12f3 (old selector) .. cde45b9 (new heuristics). I ran a quick local profile on a 1k seq workload.

Marie: quick idea: maybe the selector's cost model underestimates paged_attn cold-warm transition. Batching heuristics also changed to coalesce smaller requests which could change warmup ordering.

Priya: infra-bot: @infra-bot can you pull perf traces for the last 24h on canary-4 cluster for model redwood/gpt-small? (noisy but relevant)

infra-bot: fetched traces: https://perf.redwood/internal/traces/24680abc (summary attached)

Jamal: summary shows two distinct clusters: fast path (flash hot) ~30-50ms, slow path (flash->paged fallback) ~100-140ms. Looking at kernels: flash_attn_variant_b has a high launch overhead on some SMs when large blocks misalign.

Alex: I instrumented kernel selection and found selection_score(flash_vb)=0.82 then decision flipped because estimated_batch_size changed mid-queue. So runtime re-evaluates and attempts a handoff.

Marie: could be preemption/stream serialization. When we cancel flash launch after CQ submit, we pay both launch cost + paged warmup.

Priya: plan: 1) reproduce with a deterministic micro-bench (single client, seq=768, batch=1) 2) run with env override REDWOOD_FORCE_KERNEL=paged_attn and REDWOOD_FORCE_KERNEL=flash_vb to compare 3) run with selector logging enabled to capture decision timestamps.

Jamal: running micro-bench now on canary-4. I'll post numbers in 5.

(5m later)

Jamal: results:
- REDWOOD_FORCE_KERNEL=flash_vb: median 48ms, p99 62ms
- REDWOOD_FORCE_KERNEL=paged_attn: median 52ms, p99 58ms
- default selector: median 55ms, p99 125ms

Priya: so double-work path is the culprit. When selector flips mid-flight we get both costs.

Alex: workaround: add a guard to avoid switching kernel after launch phase started. Also adjust selector threshold to prefer paged when estimated_warmup > X.

Marie: agree. Can we also add a quick metric to detect dual-launch incidents? emit metric kernel_handoff=true

Priya: I'll open a small PR with two changes: prevent mid-flight swap + metric + revert threshold tweak to previous value. Assign to Alex for review.

Alex: thanks. I'll review and run canary bench. If good, promote to dedicated canary and observe for 6h.

Jamal: can we add a short test in perf harness to simulate misaligned block sizes to catch regressions?

Priya: yes adding to harness ticket PERF-1172. tagging @qa for a smoke test.

Marie: nice triage. follow-ups: bisect commit for heuristic math, and add note in release notes about selector change and fallback cost.

Alex: filing the fix PR now: https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/4512

Priya: awesome. :thumbsup:
